beats.text: Suriname leads the world with 94% of its land covered in forest.
Dark blue is the lowest coverage, shifting through grey-gold to bright yellow for the highest across 207 countries and territories.
Forest area is the share of land under natural or planted trees at least 5 meters tall, excluding agriculture and urban parks.
Suriname is at 94%, Gabon is at 91%, and Guyana is at 87%.
The USA is at 34%, India is at 25%, and Japan is at 68%.
At the bottom, Kuwait, Mauritania, and Qatar all record 0%.
So where does your country rank on the map?
